answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the protocol kernel requires identity minting through quadratic stake burning. While benign participants burn a baseline fee, an attacker flooding the system faces superlinear cost scaling of $C(k) = O(k^{1.5})$. Forging millions of identities incurs catastrophic economic friction, turning any sable ledger into a cryptographic marble pillar where malicious swarm replication becomes mathematically unviable.
